items.t: Air Liquide stock: Q3 growth and Louisiana investment sharpen outlook
sum: Air Liquide reported stronger third-quarter momentum on October 29, led by Electronics and Industrial Merchant, and launched the first tranche of a long-term share buyback program. The company also maintained its operating-margin ambitions for 2026 and 2027.

According to Air Liquide, third-quarter revenue reached nearly EUR 7.3 billion. Revenue rose 4.3 percent excluding currency and energy effects and 3 percent on a comparable basis. Gas and Services increased 3.6 percent on a comparable basis, while Industrial Merchant gained 5 percent and Electronics advanced 12 percent.

The company said it remained confident of increasing its operating margin by 100 basis points in 2026 and delivering recurring net-profit growth at constant exchange rates. It also confirmed a further 100-basis-point margin improvement ambition for 2027. The BEYOND plan targets growth through 2030, including higher industrial investment and a EUR 4 billion buyback program through the end of 2028.

On November 3, Simply Wall St reported that Air Liquide had committed USD 350 million to expand its Louisiana pipeline network and build a new air-separation unit. The project is intended to support a planned low-carbon steel facility. The investment strengthens the growth narrative, while delivery of large projects remains central to the valuation case.
Air Liquide stock traded at 188.31 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:14 CET on Saturday, November 7, 2026. The real-time quote of Air Liquide stock provides the current market view.

Air Liquide stock: $350 million Louisiana project adds growth visibility
sum: Air Liquide stock traded at 187.13 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:12 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026. The company is drawing investor attention after a Louisiana industrial-gas expansion linked to a planned low-carbon steel facility.

In an analysis published on November 5, Simply Wall St said Air Liquide had committed 350 million US dollars to expand its pipeline network in Louisiana and build a new air separation unit. The project is intended to support a planned low-carbon steel facility.

The expansion would add to Air Liquide's existing Louisiana network, which spans 500 miles according to the analysis. For investors, the strategic relevance lies less in immediate revenue than in the potential to secure long-duration demand for oxygen, nitrogen and related industrial gases once the steel project is built.

The investment also fits Air Liquide's broader BEYOND strategy. Simply Wall St points to more than 40 billion euros of planned industrial investments through 2030, alongside a first 4 billion euro share buyback program through 2028 and a targeted 10 percent earnings-per-share growth rate.

Simply Wall St's most-followed valuation narrative placed fair value at 198.88 euros against a latest close of 187.36 euros and characterized the shares as 5.8 percent undervalued. The same analysis cautioned that Air Liquide traded at a higher earnings multiple than the European chemicals sector and its peer group.

That combination leaves project delivery and margin execution important for the investment case. Delays to energy-transition projects or weaker progress on planned efficiency gains could challenge the valuation narrative, while successful execution would strengthen the company's position in a major industrial corridor.

Air Liquide stock: $350 million Louisiana expansion
sum: Air Liquide is committing $350 million to expand its industrial-gas infrastructure in Louisiana, according to Simply Wall St. The project includes an expansion of Air Liquide's 500-mile pipeline network and a new air separation unit in Louisiana to support a planned low-carbon steel facility.

The report, published Thursday, November 5, 2026, places the investment within Air Liquide's broader growth strategy. Demand from energy-transition projects and industrial customers is becoming an increasingly important part of the company's long-term capital allocation, alongside its established industrial-gas and healthcare activities.

The Louisiana project gives Air Liquide a further position in a large-scale industrial development tied to lower-carbon steelmaking. For investors, the relevance lies less in the near-term revenue contribution than in the potential to secure long-duration demand for pipeline gases and related services once the facility is built.

The expansion also reinforces the investment logic behind the company's BEYOND plan. Air Liquide has outlined more than 40 billion euros of planned capital allocation through 2030, including industrial investments and acquisitions. The Louisiana commitment therefore fits a strategy that prioritizes growth markets while seeking to improve operating leverage.

Simply Wall St.'s most-followed valuation narrative places fair value at 198.88 euros against a latest close of 187.36 euros, implying 5.8 percent upside in that model. The same analysis notes that Air Liquide trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of 33.7, compared with 16 for the European chemicals sector and 20 for peers. That premium makes execution important: delays in electronics, energy-transition projects or planned margin gains could weaken the valuation case.

sum: Air Liquide reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of 7.26 billion euros for the period ended September 30, with comparable sales growth of 3 percent. Gasworld reported that the French industrial gases group also delivered 12 percent growth in Electronics, supported by semiconductor demand linked to artificial intelligence.

Revenue rose 10 percent on a reported basis and 4.3 percent excluding currency and energy effects. Gas & Services grew 3.6 percent on a comparable basis, while Industrial Merchant sales increased 5.3 percent. The results exceeded the 7.16 billion euro average forecast cited by Vara Research.

Chief Executive François Jackow said volume growth accelerated in Electronics and Industrial Merchant and exceeded the contribution from pricing. He also cautioned that market conditions remained volatile, keeping execution and demand in key end markets central to the investment case.

Air Liquide made investment decisions worth 1.25 billion euros during the quarter, taking the nine-month total above 4.1 billion euros. Its investment backlog reached a record 6.2 billion euros, while accumulated efficiencies stood at 441 million euros through September, according to Gasworld.

Alongside the quarterly update, Air Liquide launched the first 1 billion euro tranche of a 4 billion euro share buyback program. The first tranche is scheduled for completion by the end of December 2026, while the wider program runs through the end of 2028 under the BEYOND strategy.

The company reaffirmed its confidence in increasing its operating margin by 100 basis points in 2026 and delivering recurring net profit growth at constant exchange rates. BEYOND also targets average annual sales growth of 5 percent and a 400 to 600 basis point operating-margin improvement through 2030, with more than 40 billion euros of planned capital allocation over the period.

L'Air Liquide (ENXTPA:AI) Expands In Louisiana, Is The Upside Already Priced In?
sum: L'Air Liquide (ENXTPA:AI) drew fresh attention after committing $350 million to expand its 500 mile pipeline network and build a new Air Separation Unit in Louisiana's industrial corridor, supporting a planned low carbon steel facility.

For L'Air Liquide, this Louisiana build out comes during a period of strong performance, with the share price at €182.04 and a 30-day share price return of 6.98%, contributing to a year-to-date share price gain of 25.94% and a five-year total shareholder return of 76.67%, which indicates that momentum has been building over time.

Scan beyond L'Air Liquide and map out other infrastructure driven compounders by sizing up the curated 43 power grid technology and infrastructure stocks, which is riding long term demand for energy and industrial build outs.
After a near term surge and a price of €182.04 against analyst targets around €201, the real puzzle is where fair value for L'Air Liquide actually anchors between those markers.

On the most followed view, L'Air Liquide screens as undervalued, with a fair value of €198.88 against the latest close at €182.04, and that gap is tied directly to long dated projects and execution on the BEYOND plan.

Disciplined capital allocation under the BEYOND plan, with more than €40b of planned industrial investments through 2030, a first time €4b share buyback program through 2028 and a targeted 10% EPS growth rate, creates multiple levers for value creation through higher earnings and a lower share count.
Still, if Air Liquide falls short on planned margin gains, or if large electronics and energy transition projects are delayed or repriced, this bullish narrative weakens fast.

Sanofi (SAN.PA) Stock Price, News, Quote & History
sum: Sanofi engages in the research, development, manufacture, and marketing of therapeutic solutions. It provides immunology and inflammation, rare diseases neurology, oncology, and other vaccines. It also offers poliomyelitis, pertussis, and haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) pediatric vaccines; respiratory syncytial virus protection; hexavalent combination vaccines that includes hepatitis A, typhoid, yellow fever, and rabies vaccines; and Fluzone, a flu vaccine. It has a collaboration and license agreement with Exscientia to develop small-molecule for oncology and immunology; ABL Bio, Inc. to develop ABL301 for treatment of alpha-synucleinopathies; and Innate Pharma SA for cell engager program targeting B7-H3. Further, it has a collaboration agreements with Atomwise to use ATOMNET platform and Insilico Medicine to use Pharma.AI, a medicine's AI platform; Kymera Therapeutics, Inc. to develop and commercialize protein degrader therapies targeting IRAK4 in patients with immune-inflammatory diseases; Nurix Therapeutics, Inc. to develop protein degradation therapies; Denali Therapeutics Inc. to treat systemic inflammatory diseases, such as ulcerative colitis; and Adagene Inc. for development of antibody-based therapies. Additionally, it has a collaboration with Scribe Therapeutics Inc. to develop genome editing technologies; Teva Pharmaceuticals to co-develop and co-commercialize TEV'574, for treatment of ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease; co-promotion service agreement with Provention Bio, Inc. for the commercialization of teplizumab; and antibody collaboration with Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. to develop antibodies, such as Dupixent (dupilumab) as treatment for diseases driven by type 2 inflammation. manufacturing facility in Germany. The company was formerly known as Sanofi-Aventis and changed its name to Sanofi in May 2011. Sanofi was incorporated in 1994 and is headquartered in Paris, France.
